description: S451 ("your recs on all five" item 1, R1 wins): the negative case for the pattern server-fn/error-boundary-fallback pins. A render-time call to a server-placed `!` function (loadName touches `?{}`, so it escalates) inside an `<errorBoundary>` is a server call in a value position — a markup `${ … }` interpolation — and is E-VALUE-SERVER-CALL (§13.7). The boundary does not exempt it: a boundary catches render-time failures of CLIENT `!` calls and host throws only (§19.6.1 / §19.6.6). Source is identical to server-fn/error-boundary-fallback. impl#1 does not emit the code (frozen; carried as g-impl1-value-server-call-s451) — it compiles the old pattern at exit 0.
rationale: §13.7 rule item 1 + normative statement: a call whose callee is server-placed SHALL NOT appear in a value position; an `<errorBoundary>` SHALL NOT exempt a value position from this rule. §19.6.6 Scope (S451): a server call SHALL NOT occur at render time.
